name: Albert Barclay
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember waiting on a staircase for my knees to settle.” On Thursday, near the downtown fountain, Albert keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I want a bench in the entry for those of us who take stairs in stages. Both bidders promised me the roof.
appearance: Albert is easy to recognize by gray hair trimmed very close behind the ears and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Albert leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations when listening.
personality: Albert has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Albert knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To win a resting bench in the entry.
family: Ashley Byrd is Albert’s first cousin once removed. Albert brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Ashley makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Ashley says, “I fitted a skirt in the salon. The client could sit while I pinned it for the first time in years.”
connections: Anna Avila. The tenant group adds a usable entry bench to the terms before backing any owner.
